requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Pushing the Limits of Block Rotations in Post-Training Quantization' — including the theoretical analysis of outlier suppression, the PeRQ framework (MassDiff permutation + block Hadamard rotation + rounding), permutation-equivariant merging, and empirical results across Llama3 and Qwen3 models under INT4/FP4/MXFP4 — have been reproduced.

verification.spec: Import the environment probe; call it and verify (a) torch.cuda.is_available() returns True and (b) at least one visible device reports total memory >= 60 GiB. Confirm the routine raises a clear error message when neither condition holds.

sub_tasks.requirements: The greedy MassDiff permutation algorithm (Algorithm 1) that calibrates a permutation to equalize the expected per-block ℓ1 norms over a calibration dataset has been implemented, using one 2048-token WikiText2 sample per permutation-equivariant region by default.

Code has been implemented that exposes a MassDiff function/class whose signature accepts a calibration activation tensor (or iterable of tensors) of shape (tokens, d) along with a block size b, and returns a permutation of the d feature coordinates (e.g., as an index array or permutation matrix).

verification.spec: Import the MassDiff callable. Verify signature via inspect.signature accepts a calibration tensor (or iterable) plus a block size b. Call with a (T=64, d=32) tensor and b=8. sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that initializes n = d/b empty blocks (each with a running ℓ1 sum of 0 and an empty coordinate list of capacity b) prior to the greedy assignment loop.

verification.spec: Inspect the MassDiff source and confirm the initialization step creates n = d/b block containers, each holding (a) a running L1-sum initialized to 0 and (b) an empty coordinate list. sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that iterates over the d feature coordinates in descending order of their expected (calibration-averaged) absolute value / mass score, consistent with a greedy mass-balancing sweep.

verification.spec: Construct a calibration tensor with known per-coordinate expected absolute values (e.g., coordinate i has E|X_i| = 100 - i for i in [0, d)). Instrument MassDiff to record the order in which coordinates are visited during the greedy sweep. Verify visit order equals descending sort by the per-coordinate mass score (i.e., i=0 first, i=d-1 last).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, at each step of the greedy loop, assigns the next coordinate to the not-yet-full block with the smallest current cumulative ℓ1 sum (ties broken deterministically), and updates that block's cumulative ℓ1 sum.

verification.spec: Import the MassDiff implementation and construct a small calibration input with known per-coordinate |X_i| means (e.g., d=8, b=4, per-coordinate masses = [10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3]). Trace the greedy loop by asserting the assignment order matches: coordinate with largest mass goes to any empty block; then subsequent coordinates go to the not-yet-full block with the smallest cumulative sum. Test tie-breaking determinism by running with identical inputs twice and asserting identical outputs. Test that the block cumulative sum is updated after each assignment (mock/spy on the update).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the capacity constraint that each of the n blocks receives exactly b coordinates, so the produced index array is a valid permutation of [d] with no repeats or omissions.

verification.spec: Call MassDiff on a calibration matrix with d=nb (e.g., d=64, b=8, n=8). Assert the returned index array has length d, contains each integer in [0, d) exactly once (numpy.unique count == d), and that when reshaped to (n, b) each block has exactly b indices. Repeat for a few (n, b) pairs including edge cases (n=1, b=1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that converts the per-block coordinate assignments into a permutation representation (index vector π and/or permutation matrix P with P e_i = e_{π(i)}) suitable for consumption by weight-merging code.

verification.spec: Verify the MassDiff API returns both an index vector pi (shape [d], dtype int) and a permutation matrix P of shape (d, d). Assert P is a valid permutation matrix (each row/column sums to 1, all entries in {0,1}) and that P @ e_i == e_{pi(i)} for all i (numeric test). Also verify P is consumable by the weight-merging code: call the merge routine with P and confirm no shape/type errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a small deterministic synthetic input (e.g., d=8, b=4, calibration matrix with known per-coordinate ℓ1 masses), the implemented MassDiff produces the greedy balanced assignment expected from Algorithm 1 (verified in a unit test comparing to a hand-computed permutation).

verification.spec: Construct a deterministic test: d=8, b=4, calibration expected |X_i| = [8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]. The optimal greedy assignment places coord 0 (mass 8) in block A, coord 1 (mass 7) in block B, then coord 2 (mass 6) into whichever has smaller current sum (block B, sum 7 < 8), etc. Hand-compute the expected permutation and assert MassDiff returns it exactly.

Assert that activation(X @ P) == activation(X) @ P elementwise (torch.allclose with rtol=1e-6). Also confirm the codebase's region-discovery logic classifies modules containing only these elementwise ops as permutation-equivariant (assert True).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies Definition 4.1 numerically: for a randomly sampled permutation P and inputs X^{(i)}, the FFN region Φ satisfies Φ(X^{(i)}P) = Φ(X^{(i)})P (elementwise, up to floating-point tolerance) on the transformer FFN subgraph implemented in the codebase.

verification.spec: Instantiate the codebase's FFN region Phi (gate_proj + up_proj + Swish + elementwise multiply). Then run the PeRQ pipeline on the region and verify that (a) the permutation P was merged into surrounding linear weights (weights differ from original), while (b) the block rotation R_tilde is still present as an online operation in the forward graph at down_proj input (e.g., a rotation hook or module remains registered).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the output-side merged weight W_tilde_2 = P^T W_2 by left-multiplying the subsequent linear layer's weight by P^T (equivalently, permuting its input rows) as prescribed by Remark 4.2.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies functional equivalence of the merged region: for random X, P and reference W_1, W_2, the output of Ψ(X) with merged weights (X · W_1 P through Φ through P^T W_2) matches the output of the original unpermuted region g_2(Φ(g_1(X))) to floating-point tolerance.

verification.spec: Implement a function compute_prop_3_2_bound(X, b) that returns sqrt(b) * max_j (||X{j}||_1 / (b * ||X{j}||_inf)) * ||X{j}||_inf; on 100 random activation vectors, assert ||XR̃||_inf <= computed bound with the block Hadamard R̃

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Corollary 3.3's deterministic evolution Z(kb', X) ≤ √k · Z(b', X) is correctly computed and empirically verified

verification.spec: Implement Z(b, X) = max_j sqrt(b) * delta{j} * ||X{j}||_inf; for at least 20 random activation vectors of dimension d=2048 and choices of b'=32, k=4, assert Z(kb', X) <= sqrt(k) * Z(b', X)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Proposition 3.4's probabilistic bound on post-rotation outliers ||XR̃||_∞ under Rademacher signs is correctly computed and verified via Monte Carlo

verification.spec: Implement the probabilistic bound from Proposition 3.4; sample Rademacher-signed vectors and empirically estimate P(||XR̃||_inf > tau); assert empirical probability of exceeding the paper's bound is ≤ epsilon (e.g., 0.05) across at least 1000 samples

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the tightest bound insight max_j ||X{j}||_∞ is minimized when max_j ||X{j}||_1 is minimized (per Equation following Prop 3.2) is correctly reflected in a MassDiff-style objective function

verification.spec: Implement mass_diff_objective(X, P, b) = max_j ||P(X){j}||_1; assert that applying MassDiff-produced permutation strictly reduces this objective vs identity permutation on calibration data

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that faithfully realizes Algorithm 1 (Mass Diffusion / MassDiff): a greedy permutation algorithm that equalizes expected block-wise ℓ1 norms across calibration tokens

verification.spec: Implement MassDiff as described in Algorithm 1; test on synthetic X where coordinates 0,1,...,d-1 have magnitudes that concentrate mass in early blocks; assert output permutation reduces max_j E[||X{j}||_1] over calibration set relative to identity by ≥ 10%

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Remark 4.2's permutation-merging identity is correctly realized: for permutation-equivariant region Ψ = g2 ∘ Φ ∘ g1, XW1 · Φ · W2 = XW̃1 · Φ · W̃2 where W̃1 = W1 P and W̃2 = P^T W2

verification.spec: Implement merge_permutation(W1, W2, P) returning (W1 @ P, P.T @ W2); construct random X, W1, W2, permutation P, and elementwise Swish activation Phi; assert numerical equivalence: g2(Phi(g1(X, W1)), W2) == g2(Phi(g1(X, W1@P)), P.T @ W2) within 1e-5

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that faithfully realizes the PeRQ quantization graph architecture in Figure 7: merged rotations R1, R2 in linear layers, online block rotation R̃3 at down projection input, merged permutations, and weight+activation quantization at all linear layers of a transformer block

verification.spec: Verify the constructed quantization graph for a single transformer block: (a) R1 and R2 are absorbed into weights (no online multiply), (b) an online block Hadamard R̃3 is inserted at the down projection input, (c) permutations P are merged into surrounding weights and not present at inference, (d) quantizers are attached at inputs/weights of all linear layers

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the INT4 quantizer defined in Appendix B (q-bit integer quantizer with step size s and zero point z, mapping real values to a discrete alphabet A ⊂ sZ with |A| ≤ 2^q) is correctly implemented and produces outputs consistent with the paper's formula on a test tensor.

verification.spec: Implement INT4 quantizer Q(x) = clip(round(x/s) + z, 0, 2^q - 1) as per Appendix B. On a fixed random tensor of shape (1024,) with known scale s=x.abs().max()/(2^(q-1)-1), assert (a) all outputs lie in {-8,...,7} after de-zero-pointing (or {0,...,15}); (b) reconstruction error scales linearly with s; (c) function is idempotent under repeated quantization.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the (MX)FP4 quantizer defined in Appendix B (standard q-bit floating-point quantizer with per-block scale and FP4 code table {±0, ±0.5, ±1, ±1.5, ±2, ±3, ±4, ±6}) is correctly implemented and its output values lie in the FP4 alphabet.

verification.spec: Implement FP4 quantizer per Appendix B: map x -> s * round_to_fp4(x/s) with FP4 codebook {±0, ±0.5, ±1, ±1.5, ±2, ±3, ±4, ±6}. For MXFP4, use group-wise scale (group=32) with power-of-2 scaling. On a random tensor, assert: (a) unique (x/s) values are subset of FP4 codebook; (b) MXFP4 scales are powers of 2; (c) group size == 32.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a full-vector normalized Hadamard rotation is applied via a butterfly O(d log d) algorithm for power-of-2 d, producing R such that R@R.T = I and ||R_i||_2 = 1

verification.spec: Import full_vector_hadamard(x); for d in [64,256,1024] draw random x; y = full_vector_hadamard(x); assert allclose(y, x @ H_d/sqrt(d)) using a reference Sylvester construction; assert orthonormality (R @ R.T == I) within 1e-5; assert operation count scales as O(d log d) via instrumentation on d=64,128,256,512 (ratio of adds within 20% of d*log2(d))
verification.paper_cite: Section 2 Structured rotations; Appendix A Remark A.1

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a block Hadamard rotation R̃ = I_n ⊗ R is applied blockwise to an activation vector X ∈ R^d with d = n·b

verification.spec: Import block_hadamard(x, b); for d=1024 and b in [16,32,128] draw random x; compute y = block_hadamard(x,b); build reference R_tilde = kron(I_{d//b}, H_b/sqrt(b)) and assert allclose(y, x @ R_tilde, atol=1e-5); assert that per-block outputs equal individual Hadamard rotations of blocks

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a non-power-of-2 Hadamard rotation is decomposed into k' = log2(k)-2 radix-2 butterfly stages followed by 2^k' 4t-dimensional rotations, with total complexity O(dt + d log k)

verification.spec: Import non_pow2_hadamard(x); for d=14336 (k=2^11, t=7) and d=9728 (k=2^9, t=19) construct reference Hadamard using known 4t base matrices; assert allclose(output, x @ H_d/sqrt(d), atol=1e-5); instrument add/subtract counts; assert count <= C*(d*t + d*log2(k)) for C=4

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Proposition 3.1 is empirically validated: whenever δ = ||X||_1/(d·||X||_∞) < 1/√d for a random activation X, applying a normalized Hadamard rotation R yields ||XR||_∞ < ||X||_∞

verification.spec: For d=1024, draw 1000 random activation vectors satisfying δ < 1/√d (e.g., near-sparse constructions); compute ||XR||_∞/||X||_∞; assert fraction with ratio < 1 equals 1.0 within tolerance; measured_value = fraction_with_suppression

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Proposition 3.2 is empirically validated: for block Hadamard R̃ = I_n ⊗ R, ||XR̃||_∞ ≤ √b · max_j δ{j} ||X{j}||_∞ holds for random activations

verification.spec: For d=1024 and b in [16,32,128], draw 1000 random activation vectors; compute LHS = ||XR̃||_∞ and RHS = sqrt(b)*max_j (||X{j}||_1 / b); assert LHS <= RHS + 1e-6 for all samples; measured_value = fraction satisfying bound

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Corollary 3.3 is empirically validated: for fixed X and b = k·b', Z(b;X) ≤ √k · Z(b';X) where Z(b;X) = max_j √b · δ{j} · ||X{j}||_∞

verification.spec: For d=1024, draw 500 random activation vectors with heavy-tailed distributions; for pairs (b',b) in [(16,64),(32,128),(64,256)], compute Z(b;X) and sqrt(k)*Z(b';X); assert fraction with Z(b;X) <= sqrt(k)*Z(b';X) equals 1.0; measured_value = fraction satisfying inequality

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Proposition 3.4 is empirically validated: for X_i = S_i Y_i with S_i iid Rademacher, ||XR̃||_∞ satisfies the sub-Gaussian tail bound with probability at least 1-ε for ε=0.05 across random Y

verification.spec: For d=1024 and b in [16,32,128,512], fix random Y of length d; draw 1000 Rademacher sign flips S; compute empirical P(||XR̃||_∞ >= tau) where tau is the sub-Gaussian bound from Prop 3.4 with ε=0.05; assert empirical failure rate <= 0.05 + 0.02 for each b; measured_value = max_b(empirical_failure_rate)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that an INT4 quantizer is available with asymmetric per-channel weight scales and per-token activation scales, computed via linear-search MSE optimization

verification.spec: Import int4_quantize_weights(W) and int4_quantize_activations(X); for a random Gaussian weight matrix W of shape [1024,1024], assert output values fall on integer grid of size 16 (2^4); assert per-channel scales are chosen via MSE linear search (verify search over >= 20 candidate scales); dequantized reconstruction ||W - W_q||_F / ||W||_F < 0.1; scales must be per-channel (one per output row) and per-token (one per input row) with asymmetric zero points

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that an FP4 (E2M1) quantizer is available with symmetric per-channel MSE weight scales and per-token ∞-norm activation scales

verification.spec: Import fp4_quantize(x, mode); verify quantized values lie in E2M1 codebook {±0, ±0.5, ±1, ±1.5, ±2, ±3, ±4, ±6}; for weight mode, verify per-channel scale minimizes MSE over linear search (>=20 candidates); for activation mode, verify scale = max(|x|)/6 per token; test on random Gaussian input of shape [128,1024] and assert reconstruction relative error < 0.15

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that an MXFP4 quantizer is available applying group-of-32 power-of-2 scaling per OCP MX specification (Rouhani et al. 2023)

verification.spec: Import mxfp4_quantize(x); for input tensor of shape [128,1024], assert grouping is applied per contiguous block of 32 along last dim; assert each group's shared scale is a power of 2 (E8M0 exponent, integer log2); assert element mantissas are from E2M1 codebook {±0,±0.5,±1,±1.5,±2,±3,±4,±6}; assert reconstruction relative error < 0.10 on random Gaussian input; verify scale = 2^floor(log2(max(|x_group|)/6))
verification.paper_cite: Section 5; Appendix B; Rouhani et al. 2023 OCP MX spec
